jobs.title: Senior Director of Operations, Care Network
jobs.description:
SHIFT:

Day (United States of America)

Seeking Breakthrough Makers

Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) offers countless ways to change lives. Our diverse community of more than 20,000 Breakthrough Makers will inspire you to pursue passions, develop expertise, and drive innovation. At CHOP, your experience is valued; your voice is heard; and your contributions make a difference for patients and families. Join us as we build on our promise to advance pediatric care—and your career. CHOP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, religion, or any other legally protected categories in any employment, training, or vendor decisions or programs. CHOP recognizes the critical importance of a workforce rich in varied backgrounds and experiences and engages in ongoing efforts to achieve that through equally varied and non-discriminatory means.

A Brief Overview

The Senior Director of Operations, Care Network, is an integral part of the Care Network Leadership team reporting to the Assistant Vice President of Operations. Working in cooperation with medical and nursing leadership. The Sr. Director of Operations, Care Network is responsible for site operations at their assigned areas, ensuring effective and efficient coordination between the administrative and clinical functions to optimize performance across the Care Network. The Sr. Director works with various departments throughout the enterprise in planning, marketing and developing new sites, services and programs. This position is accountable for the operational and financial performance and growth of the Network, meeting enterprise-wide goals relevant to the Care Network, improving community health, strengthening provider and staff engagement and improving patient and family experience. They are a champion of diversity, equity and inclusion throughout the Care Network and encourage staff development and teamwork. This role must be able to champion change and demonstrate productive and collaborative relationships throughout the Primary Care Network and with senior leadership within CHOP.

The role supervises Managers and Directors, working in tandem with the Regional Medical Directors, Nursing Directors and Managers, and other leaders within the Care Network and across the system to ensure the highest level of care and standards are met.

This leader should be able to connect with Staff, Lead with Intention and Embrace Decision Making. The role requires holistic strategic thinking, innovative and creative problem solving, and influencing abilities to advance the Care Network in growth, consumerism, talent, research and innovation and value-based care.

What You Will Do

Operational Oversight
Oversee the operational performance and achievement of annual goals for operations, finance, quality and safety, patient satisfaction and employee engagement of the assigned sites across the Care Network
Collaborate with medical and nursing leadership to establish and maintain clinical and operational standards; analyze policies, systems, procedures and space utilization and recommend innovative changes for improvement. Working with RMD and ACMO, explore opportunities to develop and implement initiatives, process improvement initiatives and new care delivery models that bring increased value and quality of care to patients and families across the Care Network.
Works collaboratively with leaders in Behavioral Health, Social Work, Care Management and other organizational colleagues to ensure the provision of the highest level of care and services for patients.
Provides leadership by partnering with other Senior Leaders in Marketing, Human Resources, Finance, Revenue Cycle, Supply Chain, MSO etc. to optimize alignment and opportunities for success.
Work with Ambulatory Leadership to develop departmental standards policies, guidelines and protocols that are implemented at site/department level.
Ensures regulatory and financial/insurance compliance relevant to the sites within their scope.
Represents the Care Network as the "face of the network" internally and externally, ensuing communication, alignment and productive collaborative relationships exist between sites/departments and the CHOP system as well as external relationships.
Financial Responsibility
Oversees the annual budget preparation and monitor fiscal performance of each area monthly, ensuring efficient and effective operations throughout the Care Network.
Accountable for the identification and implementation of financial stewardship initiatives across the Network.
Reviews P&Ls, variance analysis, LDRs ensuring team members are effectively utilizing staff, space and supplies are are working within budgetary constraints.
Works effectively as a team member with others to develop and implement new services and programs that address needs that are clinically and financially sound
Works with team members to develop and implement changes that will enhance performance of operations
Reviews data, performance and dashboards, making data driven decisions and recommendations to improve site operations and overall Network performance.
Human Resources
Works collaboratively with site leadership to recruit, retain and develop top talent. Ongoingly ensures the development of future leaders.
Regularly reviews and develops action plans to address employee and physician engagement surveys ensuring people are valued and retains a competitive market advantage.
Responsible for the recruitment, onboarding and successful engagement of site leadership. Accountable for the leadership development of their team and annually developing succession plans
Participates in the recruitment, onboarding and fostering of productive working relationships with clinical providers
Leadership
As part of the Care Network Leadership team actively participates in Network meetings and other meetings as appropriate or necessary for the efficient operations of Care Network sites.
Work with colleagues across the Care Network and enterprise to ensure alignment with enterprise goals and initiatives.
Participates in the development and implementation of strategic initiatives across the Care Network.
Participate on committees and other workgroups as requested.

Education Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree Business Administration, Health Care Administration or similar field of study Required
Master's Degree Business Administration, Health Care Administration or similar field of study Preferred

Experience Qualifications

At least eight (8) years of management experience in a healthcare setting Required

Skills And Abilities

Excellent written and verbal skills required. (Required proficiency)
Excellent analytical, financial, interpersonal, and staff relationship management skills required. (Required proficiency)
Ability to exercise a high degree of initiative, judgment, discretion and decision making to achieve organizational objectives. (Required proficiency)
Functional knowledge of group-team work dynamics; ability to create and work in strong team atmosphere. (Required proficiency)
Ability to manage and motivate all levels of employees. (Required proficiency)
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work effectively and efficiently with strict deadlines. (Required proficiency)
Familiarity with and commitment to quality/process innovation concepts and techniques. (Required proficiency)

To carry out its mission, CHOP is committed to supporting the health of our patients, families, workforce, and global community. As a condition of employment, CHOP employees who work in patient care buildings or who have patient facing responsibilities must receive an annual influenza vaccine.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Matching Services (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
About The Company

BMI is a mission-driven organization at the forefront of music rights and creator advocacy. Celebrating over 80 years of service to songwriters, composers, music publishers and businesses, BMI is a global leader in music rights management. Currently representing the public performance rights in over 25 million musical works created and owned by more than 1.4 million artists. BMI negotiates music license agreements and distributes the fees it generates as royalties to its affiliated writers and publishers when their songs are publicly performed.

About The Role

Great music depends on great matching.

As Executive Director, Matching Services, you’ll lead the strategy and operations behind one of the most critical connections in BMI’s business: accurately matching music usage to the works and rights holders it represents. You’ll oversee a broad Matching Services function supporting BMI’s core business as well as new and emerging client opportunities.

This role brings together operational leadership, data quality, technology, analytics and people leadership. You’ll drive improvements in match rates, efficiency, data integrity and royalty outcomes; advance the use of automation and machine-learning-enabled workflows; and partner across Administration, Technology, Quality Assurance and client-facing teams to strengthen BMI’s end-to-end matching capabilities.

You’ll also help shape how Matching Services evolves—balancing business value, client commitments, risk, capacity and cost while building a scalable, data-driven operation positioned to support both current needs and future growth.

Position Summary

The Executive Director, Matching Services leads the strategy, operations, and continuous improvement of BMI’s matching services function to ensure the accurate identification and matching of musical works and usage data for all BMI clients. This role drives improvements in match rates, operational efficiency, data integrity, and royalty outcomes through automation, analytics, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. The Executive Director also builds strong partnerships internally and externally to advance BMI’s overall matching capabilities and help capture new service opportunities.

Functions of the Job

Define and execute the strategy, operating model, goals, KPIs, and service expectations for Matching Services across BMI and external client work.
Prioritize work using business value, distribution impact, client commitments, strategic importance, operational risk, data readiness, deadlines, and cost-to-serve.
Lead automated and manual matching of all music usage, including exception management and unresolved-performance reduction.
Monitor productivity, accuracy, service levels, cycle time, cost per match, operational risk, and source-level trends, taking corrective action and presenting recommendations to leadership.
Partner with BMI’s Administration, Technology, and Quality Assurance teams to address upstream data-quality, metadata, registration, identifier, source-file, and timing issues that reduce match effectiveness.
Advance machine learning, semantic matching, confidence scoring, candidate ranking, automation, and human-review controls while preserving precision, auditability, and feedback loops.
Optimize BMI’s evolving mix of human and technological resources by aligning work complexity, value, time-sensitivity, capacity, and cost with the appropriate delivery model.
Support new client implementations by defining data prerequisites, matching requirements, service assumptions, exception processes, reporting, and operational readiness.
Lead and develop managers, analysts, operational teams, and extended resources through workforce planning, coaching, performance management, training, succession planning, documentation, and continuous improvement.
Serve as the senior Matching Services subject matter expert, communicating priorities, tradeoffs, risks, investment needs, and results across executive, business, technical, and client-facing stakeholders.
Contribute to new business pursuits by offering subject matter expertise, demonstrations, and proof-of-concept work in partnership with other BMI teams.
Oversee claiming, rights identification, usage matching, invoicing, and reconciliation against consumption files to ensure accurate attribution, monetization, revenue collection, and distribution.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly and indirectly manages managers, analysts, operational staff, and extended labor resources supporting Matching Services.
Responsible for hiring, coaching, performance management, development planning, succession planning, workforce planning, and training strategy.
Accountable for building the leadership, analytical, technical, and operational capabilities required for a more automated, data-driven, and globally scalable matching function.

Position Qualification Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Music Business, Operations Management, or related field required.
Master’s degree preferred.

Experience

10+ years of progressively responsible experience in operations, administration, royalty processing, rights management, data management, matching/identification, including significant leadership experience.
Significant experience leading complex operational teams, process transformation, data-quality improvement, and technology-enabled workflow optimization.
Experience managing prioritization across multiple business lines, client commitments, service levels, and resource constraints.
Experience working with large-scale data environments, matching systems, machine-learning-enabled workflows, or advanced operational analytics preferred.
Experience supporting music rights administration, royalty distributions, Audio usage, Audio Visual usage, global administration, or external client-service models preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong strategic planning, operational leadership, and portfolio prioritization skills.
Demonstrated ability to make nuanced value judgments that consider revenue impact, strategic importance, risk, client commitments, and resource cost.
Deep understanding of data quality management, copyright/repertoire dependencies, operational controls, and usage-to-work matching concepts.
Strong understanding of automation, machine learning, confidence-based decisioning, human-in-the-loop review models, and scalable process design.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the ability to connect operational outcomes to cost, ROI, quality, and business value.
Ability to influence and collaborate across multiple departments, leadership levels, technical teams, operational groups, and client-facing stakeholders.
Strong communication and executive presentation skills, including the ability to explain tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations clearly.
Knowledge of music rights administration, performance processing, royalty distributions, metadata management, Audio usage, Audio Visual usage, or global administration preferred.
Experience with business intelligence tools, reporting platforms, operational analytics, and process-performance measurement preferred.

What Success Looks Like

You establish a clear strategy and operating model for Matching Services, with meaningful goals, KPIs and service expectations that connect day-to-day work to business outcomes.
You improve match rates, data integrity, service levels and operational efficiency while maintaining the precision, controls and auditability required for royalty-related work.
You use data, analytics and sound judgment to prioritize work based on business value, distribution impact, client commitments, risk, readiness, deadlines and cost.
You identify where automation, machine learning and human review can work together to create a more scalable and effective matching operation.
You build strong partnerships across Administration, Technology, Quality Assurance and client-facing teams to address upstream issues that affect matching outcomes.
You develop strong leaders and teams, strengthening the analytical, technical and operational capabilities needed for a more automated, data-driven and globally scalable function.
You communicate complex tradeoffs, risks, investment needs and recommendations clearly to executive, technical, operational and client-facing stakeholders.
You help position Matching Services to support new clients, emerging business opportunities and continued growth without losing focus on BMI’s core distribution responsibilities.

Why Join Us?

Matching is where data becomes value.

At BMI, accurately connecting music usage to the right works and rights holders is essential to royalty distribution and to the service we provide songwriters, composers, publishers and clients. As Executive Director, Matching Services, you’ll have the opportunity to shape a function that sits at the intersection of music rights, data, technology and operations.

You’ll lead meaningful transformation—strengthening today’s matching performance while helping build a more automated, analytical and scalable model for the future. Your work will influence royalty outcomes, operational effectiveness, client service and BMI’s ability to pursue new opportunities.

If you’re energized by complex operational challenges, developing high-performing teams, using technology and data to improve outcomes, and building solutions that support the people and businesses behind music, we’d love to meet you!

Benefits & Perks

We take care of our people, here’s what you can expect when joining the team:

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
401K with employer match on 100% of the first 4%.
Flexible Spending Accounts
Hybrid Office Schedule & Remote Friday's
Short-Term & Long-Term Disability Benefits
Paid Vacation & Sick/Personal Time
Paid Volunteer Time Off
12 Paid Holidays
Summer Half-Days
Company Paid Life Insurance
Up To 12 weeks Paid Parental Leave
Tuition Assistance Program
Commuter Benefits (New York)
Employee Resource Groups
Entertainment discounts and access to BMI concerts and events in our offices
Employee appreciation events and holiday parties hosted at all office locations
